LQRAfJyEsko.summary: Dominion is a two-hour documentary using drones and hidden cameras to expose conditions in animal agriculture, including food, clothing, entertainment and research. It questions humanity's dominion over animals.
LQRAfJyEsko.why: HN commenters push it, often forcefully, as the video to watch to see what factory farming really involves, and some say it changed their diet.

L0KuAx1COEk.summary: Zach Hartwig of MIT introduces the key concepts of magnetic fusion energy and the state of fusion research. He then presents MIT's proposed pathway of using high-field superconducting magnets to build smaller, cheaper tokamaks on a climate-relevant timescale.
L0KuAx1COEk.why: Recommended again and again as the best accessible overview of fusion physics, useful for judging fusion announcements and understanding why high-temperature superconducting magnets matter.

LIb3L4vKZ7U.summary: Andrei Alexandrescu's CppCon 2015 talk argues that std::allocator is badly designed. He proposes building high-performance allocators from small composable, templated pieces.
LIb3L4vKZ7U.why: HN repeatedly recommends it as an entertaining, mind-opening talk on allocator design and composable generic programming.

LnzuMJLZRdU.summary: Ben Eater starts a series building a working computer on breadboards around the 6502 microprocessor. In this first part he gets a 'hello world' running from scratch.
LnzuMJLZRdU.why: HN repeatedly recommends it as the best hands-on way to understand how a CPU and a computer work from first principles.

LkH2r-sNjQs.summary: Tom Scott explains why electronic voting is a bad idea. Elections must be trusted by everyone and attacks on software scale in ways attacks on paper do not, so open source or blockchain fixes do not solve it.
LkH2r-sNjQs.why: HN treats it as the go-to layperson-friendly argument against e-voting and links it in nearly every voting-technology thread.

LrObZ_HZZUc.summary: CGP Grey explains that the City of London is a tiny, separate entity with its own governance, history and privileges, distinct from the city called London. He covers its financial role and how it is run.
LrObZ_HZZUc.why: HN's go-to short explainer for the City of London versus London, cited in many finance and UK threads.

LKtk3HCgTa8.summary: Rich Hickey's Strange Loop 2011 keynote separates 'simple' (not intertwined) from 'easy' (familiar or near at hand) and argues that software complexity comes from complecting things. It offers a vocabulary for judging designs and abstractions.
LKtk3HCgTa8.why: It is one of HN's most frequently recommended programming talks, cited whenever people debate complexity, simplicity and abstraction, and valued well beyond Clojure.

LA_DrBwkiJA.summary: Tom7 explains how he built a SIGBOVIK 2017 paper made only of printable ASCII bytes that is also a valid DOS executable. He writes a C compiler targeting printable x86 without self-modifying code and solves the puzzles the constraint creates.
LA_DrBwkiJA.why: HN fans call it a favorite engineering video and a showcase of Tom7's masterpiece-level, playful hacking.

LJ4W1g-6JiY.summary: Sabine Hossenfelder explains how close nuclear fusion really is to break-even, and why headlines about ITER and lab milestones are misleading. She distinguishes plasma gain (Q plasma) from whole-system gain (Q total) and shows the latter is still far below one.
LJ4W1g-6JiY.why: HN commenters post it under nearly every fusion breakthrough story as the standard reality check on Q-factor hype.

Ll6-eGDpimU.summary: Technology Connections explains dishwasher detergent use, arguing people use too much and that powder beats pods and gels. It follows an earlier dishwasher video and covers enzymes, bleach, rinse aids and when salt is needed.
Ll6-eGDpimU.why: HN regards the dishwasher videos as must-watch practical explainers, linked whenever dishwashers, detergents or pods come up.

LO1mTELoj6o.summary: CGP Grey's sarcastic animated video adapted from the book How to Be Miserable, listing habits that reliably make people unhappy. By inverting the advice, it shows what to avoid and prompts reflection on goals and routines.
LO1mTELoj6o.why: HN recommends it widely in advice threads on depression, habits, and goal setting as a funny, memorable way to see what to do by seeing what not to do.

LPjzfGChGlE.summary: Roy Beck's short gumball presentation using World Bank and Census data to argue that letting people immigrate to the US cannot solve world poverty because the numbers are so large. It is made by NumbersUSA, an immigration-restriction advocacy group.
LPjzfGChGlE.why: HN commenters recommend it as a quick visualization of the scale of global poverty versus immigration capacity, though it is advocacy with a specific viewpoint.

LMbI6sk-62E.summary: Isaac Arthur explains the orbital ring, a megastructure launch-assist system that could move bulk cargo cheaply to orbit and beyond. He compares it with space elevators and discusses power transmission.
LMbI6sk-62E.why: HN commenters offer it as the likely future of cheap access to space, feasible without exotic materials.

LxgMdjyw8uw.summary: Kurzgesagt's animated take on climate change argues that, despite alarming headlines, there are real reasons for hope as technology, policy and public attitudes shift. It surveys trends and solutions while acknowledging the scale of the problem.
LxgMdjyw8uw.why: HN commenters recommend it as an articulate, uplifting counterweight to climate doomerism, though one critic calls it a form of denialism and another notes it omits nuclear.

LKnqECcg6Gw.summary: MinutePhysics explains that computers store brightness nonlinearly, so blurring and blending colors in raw RGB gives wrong, dark results. It shows why mixed colors, such as in gradients, look off.
LKnqECcg6Gw.why: HN cites it as the accessible go-to explanation of gamma and color blending errors in image programs.

L5pUA3LsEaw.summary: Robert Miles asks whether corporations can be thought of as artificial general superintelligences and how far the analogy holds. He argues the differences, such as being limited by employees' capabilities, matter for AI safety.
L5pUA3LsEaw.why: HN points to it as an accessible rebuttal to the claim that AI risk is just corporate risk.

LEZv-kQUSi4.summary: Stuart Halloway's satirical talk describes how to protect yourself from industry change by spreading complexity through systems while following idiomatic practice. It uses this inversion to catalog software design anti-patterns.
LEZv-kQUSi4.why: HN commenters love it as a witty and insightful tour of design anti-patterns, applicable to DSLs, OOP and API design.

LQmTKxI4Wn4.summary: A short Harvard Online animated lesson on how the mitochondrial electron transport chain works. It shows proton pumping and the machinery that drives ATP synthesis.
LQmTKxI4Wn4.why: HN commenters share it to show how cells work as nanoscale machines, which many find mind-blowing.

LRhbcDzbGSU.summary: Jason Scott discusses making his documentary GET LAMP at a Google Tech Talk and screens part of the film. It covers the history of text adventures and interactive fiction, with interviews of Infocom developers and others.
LRhbcDzbGSU.why: HN recommends it to anyone interested in text adventures, Infocom, MUDs and early computer gaming history.

LbH1ZDImaI8.summary: Everyday Astronaut explains the basic physics of rocket engines, the main engine cycles and fuel types, then compares SpaceX's methane-fueled full-flow staged combustion Raptor to other engines. It runs nearly 50 minutes with chapter markers.
LbH1ZDImaI8.why: HN commenters send people here as the best accessible starting point for understanding why Raptor and fuel choice matter for Starship.

Ljzj9Msli5o.summary: Astronaut Mike Mullane explains normalisation of deviance, where teams gradually come to accept violations of their own safety standards. He uses the Challenger shuttle disaster as the main case, drawing on NASA's ignored warnings before the launch. It is the first part of a talk given to a fire-fighters' association.
Ljzj9Msli5o.why: HN commenters cite it whenever a thread involves ignored warnings, shortcuts or routine risk, as the clearest introduction to the concept.

LtFyP0qy9XU.summary: A clip from the 2011 film Margin Call in which a firm's CEO, played by Jeremy Irons, tells a senior executive about the cycles of financial crashes. Kevin Spacey's character says he wants out, and the scene ends on the line that it is just money.
LtFyP0qy9XU.why: HN shares it in bubble and crash threads as a memorable scene about market cycles and about information work versus physical labor.

L-x8DYTOv7w.summary: Tom Scott examines why YouTubers must declare paid endorsements while TV, film and other media face no such rule, comparing regulations in the UK and US.
L-x8DYTOv7w.why: HN cites it as a clear explainer on sponsorship and ad disclosure rules and their inconsistency across media.

LWGJA9i18Co.summary: OK Go's music video for Upside Down & Inside Out, filmed during parabolic flights so the band and performers are weightless in the plane.
LWGJA9i18Co.why: Commenters recommend it as a creative music video shot entirely in zero gravity, citing it in threads about parabolic flights and space.

L1j93RnIxEo.summary: Zack Freedman gives advice on why makers fail to finish projects, including scrapping bad ideas, showing work publicly and writing a plan that keeps projects fun. It is aimed at hardware DIY but generalizes.
L1j93RnIxEo.why: HN finds the project-scoping rubric useful for programmers too and recommends it on finishing side projects.

L_XJ_s5IsQc.summary: A live, overdub-free performance of 'Lingus' by Snarky Puppy, from the 'We Like It Here' DVD recorded in Utrecht. It features a Cory Henry keyboard solo.
L_XJ_s5IsQc.why: HN commenters recommend Snarky Puppy as proof that vibrant, progressive modern jazz is being made today.

LnS0PfNyj4U.summary: Dr. Russell Barkley explains how different ADHD medications work and how they differ from one another, in a short clip.
LnS0PfNyj4U.why: HN recommends Barkley as the best resource on ADHD, with clear explanations of what prescription ADHD drugs do.

L3LMbpZIKhQ.summary: The first lecture of MIT 6.042J Mathematics for Computer Science, taught by Tom Leighton, introducing mathematical proofs. It covers propositions, implication and basic proof methods.
L3LMbpZIKhQ.why: HN users recommend it as a good discrete math course for programmers, praising Leighton's relatable stories that motivate new concepts.

LNidsMesxSE.summary: David Rosen of Wolfire Games explains how simple procedural techniques can produce fluid, interactive character animation from very few keyframes. Examples come from Overgrowth, Receiver and Black Shades, from his 2014 GDC session.
LNidsMesxSE.why: HN points to it as a concrete case of procedural animation that keeps characters responsive, often in threads about Overgrowth and game feel.

LUFp6sjKbkE.summary: A full-day recording of the University of Utah computer science department's 50th anniversary event with panels, keynotes and talks by alumni and pioneers. It includes Ivan Sutherland's presentation on single flux quantum electronics.
LUFp6sjKbkE.why: HN points to specific segments, especially Sutherland's SFQ talk and graphics pioneers, rather than the full seven hours.

LZgyVadkgmI.summary: Lichess founder Thibault Duplessis talks at Big Techday 10 in Munich about how Lichess works and how he built it. He covers the project's origins and technical challenges including cheating detection.
LZgyVadkgmI.why: HN commenters point to it as a good talk on how one person built a major free, open-source chess server with few resources, and on the cheating problem.

LfascZSTU4o.summary: A 2006 television appearance in which Peter Schiff warns on Kudlow & Co about the housing bubble and an approaching US economic collapse.
LfascZSTU4o.why: Offered as an example of someone who publicly predicted the financial crisis ahead of time, in arguments about economic forecasting.

Lq-Y7crQo44.summary: AlphaPhoenix uses Monte Carlo simulation and annealing-style methods to draw North Carolina congressional district maps, both gerrymandered and fair. He focuses on the fascinating computational problem rather than the politics.
Lq-Y7crQo44.why: HN recommends it as an entertaining demonstration of how powerful algorithmic gerrymandering can be.

LruaD7XhQ50.summary: CGP Grey explains what it means that a third of the United States is federally owned land. It describes the agencies that manage it and why so much of it is in the western states.
LruaD7XhQ50.why: Offered as the quick, clear explainer on US federal land ownership whenever land use in the West comes up.

LsGZ_2RuJ2A.summary: The first episode of Ian Hubert's Dynamo Dream series, a one-person sci-fi short made in Blender with a gritty futuristic city setting. It was made with help from friends and Patreon supporters over about three years.
LsGZ_2RuJ2A.why: HN holds it up as an impressive example of what a tiny team can achieve with Blender.

LwicN2u6Dro.summary: Stephen Kell's Strange Loop talk argues that C and Unix already contain Smalltalk-like dynamism and introspection that can be exposed. He presents his liballocs research on bridging dynamic and compiled languages.
LwicN2u6Dro.why: HN commenters recommend it in Smalltalk and Unix threads as a demonstration of runtime dynamism hiding in native binaries and shared libraries.

LKJBND_IRdI.summary: This Place argues that the uncanny valley is a flawed concept, since 'human likeness' is too broad and the supporting evidence is cherry-picked. It proposes that the creepiness really comes from how animated characters and robots move.
LKJBND_IRdI.why: Recommended as a convincing counterargument to the widely repeated idea of the uncanny valley.

LS3GQk9ETRU.summary: Tech Ingredients explains the principles of magnetohydrodynamics and builds several demonstrations, including propelling liquid metal and electrolytes with magnets and a railgun-style setup.
LS3GQk9ETRU.why: It comes up as a great explainer on magnetohydrodynamic drives and pumps in threads about silent submarine propulsion.

LSX3qdy0dFg.summary: Sacha Arnoud, Waymo's Director of Engineering, gives a lecture in MIT's 2018 deep learning for self-driving cars course on the rise of machine learning in autonomous vehicles. It covers how Waymo uses deep learning and how it handles tricky driving situations.
LSX3qdy0dFg.why: Pointed to during self-driving news threads as an insider view of Waymo's progress, deep learning's role and its limits.

Le7Fqbsrrm8.summary: Astronomer David Kipping of Cool Worlds talks with Mick West to break down the three declassified Pentagon UFO videos. They explain the footage through camera artifacts, glare, and perspective effects.
Le7Fqbsrrm8.why: HN recommends it as the boring, convincing debunking of the Gofast, FLIR and Gimbal videos, which commenters say ended UFO hype for them.

LmpuerlbJu0.summary: Kurzgesagt's animated explainer on the human immune system, describing the body as an ecosystem and how immune defenses cope with the variety of invaders. It promotes their book Immune.
LmpuerlbJu0.why: HN users call it a mind-blowing and good explainer on how the immune system works, and cite it in vaccine and disease threads.

Ly6USRwTHe0.summary: A short demo of an open-source Krita plugin that uses Stable Diffusion to generate and edit images in place. It adds ControlNet scribble and line-art support. You select an area, push a button, and new matching content appears.
Ly6USRwTHe0.why: HN recommends it as a quick way to see how the Krita AI plugin works and how it matches Photoshop's generative features.

L2IKCdnzl5k.summary: Engineering Explained compares the lifecycle emissions of keeping an old car with those of buying a new, more efficient one. It weighs manufacturing emissions against emissions from driving, and covers gas versus electric cars.
L2IKCdnzl5k.why: HN commenters cite it in EV and emissions debates for its numbers on when replacing a car pays off.

L41oIvre9K0.summary: Casey Muratori captures CygnusEd Professional running on an Amiga 2000, showing how smoothly it scrolled text. He notes the real effect is better on a period CRT.
L41oIvre9K0.why: It is cited as evidence that text scrolling on late-80s hardware was smoother than in many modern editors.

L9n77DPJ7AE.summary: Anders Puck Nielsen clears up common misunderstandings about what legally counts as genocide, then compares the situation in Gaza with the genocide case against Putin. The chapters cover the definition, individual intent, and the two case comparisons.
L9n77DPJ7AE.why: HN commenters recommend it as an accessible, level-headed explanation of the UN definition of genocide in heated Gaza threads, though one notes it omits some context.

LIIBRr31DIU.summary: Home video from 1993 showing Future Crew members at Mika Tuomi's home finishing the PC demo Second Reality shortly before release.
LIIBRr31DIU.why: HN people share it as rare behind-the-scenes footage of the making of a legendary demoscene production.

LKiBlGDfRU8.summary: Sabine Hossenfelder explains why she left academia, criticizing its incentives, funding and career structure. She gives a personal account of the social problems in science.
LKiBlGDfRU8.why: HN users cite it in threads about academia, grant incentives, fraud and women-only programs, often as an eye-opening personal take.

LKp2gikIkD8.summary: Folding Ideas examines weird, algorithm-gamed children's content on YouTube, from automated toddler videos and educational spam to exploitative prank channels. It looks at how autoplay and recommendation systems reward this material.
LKp2gikIkD8.why: HN people cite it as an eye-opening summary of Elsagate and the manipulation of YouTube's algorithm in threads about bot-made and kids' content.

LLCF7vPanrY.summary: Isao Hashimoto's time-lapse map shows all 2053 nuclear explosions between 1945 and 1998, with each nation getting a blip and a running tally. Each second represents one month.
LLCF7vPanrY.why: Used as a striking visualization of the sheer scale and rhythm of nuclear testing, and as a model for conveying scale with a counter.

LMxate9gegg.summary: Remastered episode of Tim Hunkin's The Secret Life of Machines about the radio, covering its development including Hertz and Marconi experiments and Armstrong's FM radio in animated form.
LMxate9gegg.why: HN recommends the series as awesome and notes it is now legally on YouTube; commenters cite it for radio history.

LNjJTgXujno.summary: Peter Norvig, then Director of Research at Google, talks at Startup School 2008 about leveraging large amounts of data and about technical challenges in Google projects such as image search. A central idea is that data can beat hand-written programming.
LNjJTgXujno.why: HN points to it as a source for Norvig's 'unreasonable effectiveness of data' argument and for his views on image search and the semantic web.

LPqtfC70QTU.summary: The Quantified Scientist, a sleep researcher, tests Apple Watch sleep tracking against a research-grade Dreem 2 headband, comparing accuracy for sleep stages, deep and REM sleep. The review is data-focused rather than feature-focused.
LPqtfC70QTU.why: HN commenters cite it as evidence that Apple Watch is the most accurate consumer sleep tracker and trust the channel for its scientific approach.

LZPKTaVB1IU.summary: Dr. Layne Norton critiques claims made by Dr. Robert Lustig on the Huberman Lab podcast, going through them against the nutrition research with cited sources. It covers topics like sugar, calories and fruit juice.
LZPKTaVB1IU.why: Linked as a rebuttal when Lustig's or similar influencer nutrition claims come up.

LabqeJEOQyI.summary: Clay Shirky argues at Web 2.0 Expo NY that the problem online is not information overload but filter failure. He says the real challenge is building better ways to filter and organize what we see.
LabqeJEOQyI.why: HN invokes it as a reframing of the information overload problem, often when discussing content filtering, tagging and curation.

LdOe18KhtT4.summary: John Allspaw and Paul Hammond's Velocity 09 talk on how Flickr achieved ten or more deploys per day through close cooperation between development and operations.
LdOe18KhtT4.why: HN regards it as a pivotal early talk in the DevOps movement and the original source for the idea.

Lg_aUOSLuRo.summary: Tech Ingredients demonstrates how microwaves work and how they affect objects at range, then shows ways to defend against them. It includes a correction about rectifier output frequency.
Lg_aUOSLuRo.why: HN commenters recommend it as a practical explanation of microwave hazards and shielding, and of using microwave ovens safely without an enclosure.

LmlAYnFF_s8.summary: Thunderf00t presents high-speed camera footage of alkali metals such as sodium and NaK reacting with water. The footage shows that the explosion is not caused by hydrogen ignition, as the usual explanation says. It is a Coulomb explosion driven by electrons leaving the metal.
LmlAYnFF_s8.why: HN links it as the accessible video explanation of the sodium-in-water research, and when Coulomb explosions or sodium batteries come up.

LtlrITxB5qg.summary: CuriousMarc runs the program 'Edith' on a 1959 IBM 1401 mainframe at the Computer History Museum. The program prints a famous line-printer image on the vintage machine. The video is part retro-computing demo and part joke.
LtlrITxB5qg.why: HN points to it as a fun, well-known example of line-printer art on early IBM hardware, and to the channel for vintage computing history.

Lu56xVlZ40M.summary: Two Minute Papers covers OpenAI's multi-agent hide-and-seek experiment, in which agents learned emergent tool use and found ways to break the game's rules. It summarizes the 'Emergent Tool Use from Multi-Agent Interaction' paper.
Lu56xVlZ40M.why: HN mentions it as a fun and slightly worrying example of AI systems behaving in unintended ways when optimizing.

L-s_3b5fRd8.summary: Kevin Rose interviews Elon Musk in 2012 about his companies PayPal, SpaceX and Tesla. It includes Musk's short explanation of reasoning from first principles versus by analogy.
L-s_3b5fRd8.why: HN pointed people to it for the original interview and Musk's concise take on first-principles thinking.

L43-XE1uwWc.summary: Michael Levin's keynote at the ALife 2020 conference, 'Robot Cancer', on how bioelectric signaling in embryogenesis and regeneration informs unconventional computing, cognition and the 'software of life'. He argues biology offers lessons for building adaptive machines.
L43-XE1uwWc.why: HN readers point to it as a companion to other Levin material on bioelectricity, goal-directedness in cells and cancer as a breakdown in cell communication.

L6A1Lt0kvMA.summary: Destin Sandlin of Smarter Every Day explains 'Facebook freebooting', where Facebook users re-upload YouTubers' videos natively and the original creators lose views and revenue. He describes his own attempts to get Facebook to act.
L6A1Lt0kvMA.why: HN cites it as the first-hand account of video piracy on Facebook whenever the platform's treatment of creators comes up.

LA-gNoxSLCE.summary: John Graham-Cumming of Cloudflare talks at dotScale 2015 about handling roughly 10 trillion log lines a month. The talk touches on Cloudflare's hardware, its logging stack and its use of Lua in Nginx.
LA-gNoxSLCE.why: Mostly cited as a source for details of Cloudflare's architecture, such as LuaJIT-based request inspection and request volumes.

LCEmiRjPEtQ.summary: Andrej Karpathy's keynote at AI Startup School laying out software 1.0, 2.0 and 3.0, with LLMs seen as utilities, fabs and operating systems. It covers LLM quirks, partial-autonomy apps and keeping a human in the generate-and-verify loop.
LCEmiRjPEtQ.why: HN mostly cites it as a source for Karpathy's framing of programming in English and his generate-then-verify workflow, with a few critics finding it hype.

LDPMpc-ENqY.summary: Stephan T. Lavavej's GoingNative 2013 talk explaining why calling rand() and using rand() % 100 is bad in C++, and how the C++11 <random> header does the job properly.
LDPMpc-ENqY.why: It is the standard reference for why rand() is broken in C++ and what to use instead.

LDW0QWie21s.summary: Greg Young, who coined CQRS, looks back on a decade of domain-driven design, CQRS and event sourcing at DDD Europe 2016. He discusses where event sourcing applies and how simple its core can be.
LDW0QWie21s.why: HN commenters cite it in event sourcing threads for Young's views on when to use it, including advice against cross-application event sourcing.

LEENEFaVUzU.summary: A Kurzgesagt animation on longtermism, arguing that because the future could hold trillions of people, our actions' effect on future generations may be what matters most.
LEENEFaVUzU.why: HN uses it as a reference for the scale of future human population and long-term thinking.

LHvR1fRTW8g.summary: A three-minute minutephysics video on the orbital mechanics of why crashing into the Sun takes far more energy than leaving the solar system.
LHvR1fRTW8g.why: HN links it as the quick explanation of why you cannot just throw things into the Sun.

LSxbc1IN9Gg.summary: Linus Sebastian of Linus Tech Tips discloses that he has invested in Framework, the modular repairable laptop maker. He explains his reasoning and the commitments he is making to viewers about future coverage.
LSxbc1IN9Gg.why: HN cites it as Linus's own explanation of why he invested in Framework and why outside investment suits a hardware company.

LUCCR4jAS3Y.summary: A recording of the leaked 2014 phone call between US diplomat Victoria Nuland and ambassador Geoffrey Pyatt about the future of Ukraine's government, republished by The Tribune.
LUCCR4jAS3Y.why: HN commenters cite it as primary-source audio in geopolitical arguments about US involvement in Ukraine, favoring listening to the call over reading the transcript.

LY7x2Ihqjmc.summary: Sunspring is a sci-fi short film starring Thomas Middleditch. Its screenplay was written by an LSTM neural network trained on sci-fi scripts, and the team shot and edited it in 48 hours.
LY7x2Ihqjmc.why: HN cites it as an early, quirky example of machine-generated screenplays and what LSTMs could do.

LZAeZBVAzVw.summary: A 95-minute recorded debate at the ARITH23 computer arithmetic conference between John Gustafson, proponent of unums/posits, and William Kahan, architect of IEEE 754 floating point. They argue the merits of the new number formats versus conventional floats and interval arithmetic.
LZAeZBVAzVw.why: It is the go-to primary source whenever HN discusses posits versus IEEE floats, valued for Kahan's sharp critique despite the poor audio.

LhQlwKX3LQA.summary: Footage shot with a Nikon P1000 superzoom camera showing extreme optical zoom on distant targets from Ben Lomond in Scotland.
LhQlwKX3LQA.why: Cited as an eye-opening demonstration of how much a consumer camera can resolve at long range, relevant to privacy and surveillance threads.

LiWlvBro9eI.summary: A clip of the Yes Men posing as a Dow Chemical spokesman on the BBC and announcing compensation for victims of the Bhopal disaster, a hoax on live television.
LiWlvBro9eI.why: HN cites it as a favorite example of a famous prank or trolling stunt that fooled a major broadcaster.

LikxFZZO2sk.summary: A short Boston Dynamics clip of the Atlas humanoid robot doing parkour, jumping over a log and leaping up steps using whole-body control and computer vision to locate markers.
LikxFZZO2sk.why: HN cites it as a striking demonstration of how far humanoid robot agility had come.

LkYB931iUjc.summary: Dave2D looks at why MacBook speakers sound so much better than those on other laptops, with input from an audio researcher. He compares them against the best Windows laptop speakers.
LkYB931iUjc.why: Cited as support for the common claim that MacBook speakers are far ahead of other laptops.

LpGA2fmAHvM.summary: Joel Spolsky's 2012 Google tech talk on the cultural anthropology of Stack Overflow and Stack Exchange. He explains how the software was designed to shape community norms and curation standards.
LpGA2fmAHvM.why: HN points to it to explain that Stack Overflow's strict moderation was deliberate design, not accident.

LseK5gp66u8.summary: Tom Scott explains how decades of deep coal mining sank parts of Germany's Ruhr Valley and changed its drainage. Pumps run by Emschergenossenschaft must now work permanently to keep towns and cities from flooding.
LseK5gp66u8.why: HN uses it as a well-known example of infrastructure that must run forever to keep an area habitable.

LtITDtZPYEw.summary: In a CNBC interview with Becky Quick, Warren Buffett explains why he sees bitcoin as an asset that produces nothing. He contrasts it with productive assets such as a farm.
LtITDtZPYEw.why: HN links it as the primary source for Buffett's bitcoin views and his argument about productive versus non-productive assets.

L1N3WXZ_1LM.summary: A French comedy sketch-song by Les Inconnus parodying wealthy young people from Auteuil, Neuilly and Passy by mimicking the style of banlieue rap.
L1N3WXZ_1LM.why: HN mostly uses it as a joke or cultural reference for rich Parisian stereotypes and subcultures, rather than recommending it.

L1UgdoP2aeg.summary: A Seeker short documentary on a lab where robots run experiments with almost no human intervention, covering automation and active machine learning in drug discovery and synthetic biology.
L1UgdoP2aeg.why: HN cites it as an example of automated cloud labs and AI already running physical experiments.

L2zqTYgcpfg.summary: A short EDS television commercial that shows an airplane being built while it is in flight. It is an early use of the 'building the plane as it flies' metaphor.
L2zqTYgcpfg.why: HN mentions it mainly as the origin of the phrase about rebuilding a plane mid-flight, usually applied to software projects.

L3LbxDZRgA4.summary: A short Simpsons clip from Who Shot Mr. Burns Part 1 in which Mr. Burns declares the sun his enemy and plans to block it out.
L3LbxDZRgA4.why: Quoted as a joke whenever sunshades, geoengineering or anti-solar policy come up.

L3dxMGzt5mU.summary: A one-minute clip from Ricky Gervais's 2018 Netflix special in which he riffs on people getting offended by internet commentary, framed as 'guitar lessons' in humanity. It is a short stand-up excerpt.
L3dxMGzt5mU.why: HN uses it as a joke or sarcastic reference, usually in reply to earnest or self-help-style posts, rather than recommending it as something to learn from.

L5foZIKuEWQ.summary: A short clip from The Matrix in which Agent Smith tells Morpheus that humans behave like a virus. It is shared as a standalone monologue.
L5foZIKuEWQ.why: HN commenters link it as a quip or reference when threads touch on human impact on the planet.

L75ESD9PBOw.summary: Footage of the first manned flight of an electric multicopter, flown by Volocopter (then e-volo) in October 2011. The 90-second flight was a Guinness World Record.
L75ESD9PBOw.why: HN points to it as proof that manned multicopters and eVTOL craft existed well before the current hype.

L9oh3gqOEKU.summary: A short Flash animation made in 2001 by an IBM employee, set to the company's old 'Ever Onward' rally song, with imagery from IBM history.
L9oh3gqOEKU.why: It is linked as an audio and visual example of IBM's corporate rally songs in threads about IBM culture.

LCIsIfEOEI8.summary: A real-time demoscene production made with an overhead projector, released by DESiRE and TRSi for @Party in the OHP category. It is a short, quirky entry in the demoscene tradition.
LCIsIfEOEI8.why: Mentioned as a quirky example of demoscene creativity and related overhead-projector techniques.

LD0x7ho_IYc.summary: Vsauce looks at 'juvenoia', the exaggerated fear that new media and youth culture are corrupting the young. It gives historical examples of older generations complaining about the next one.
LD0x7ho_IYc.why: HN uses it to put worries about phones, music and technology and kids into historical perspective.

LFrdqQZ8FFc.summary: A Monty Python sketch about the Royal Society for Putting Things on Top of Other Things.
LFrdqQZ8FFc.why: Cited as a joke whenever something is stacked or oddly named.

LM0T6hLH15k.summary: A short Magic Leap promo clip of a whale breaching through a gym floor in mixed reality.
LM0T6hLH15k.why: Cited mostly critically as the infamous whale demo that overstated what the Magic Leap hardware could deliver.

LM8kLaJ2NDU.summary: Footage of the 2007 Aurora test, in which a cyberattack was used to destroy a large generator at a test facility in Idaho.
LM8kLaJ2NDU.why: HN cites it as proof that cyberattacks can physically destroy power grid equipment.

LMmdl4VltD4.summary: A CollegeHumor sketch from the Hardly Working series in which a pair of startup founders pitch a website using incomprehensible buzzwords and branding nonsense. It parodies Silicon Valley startup culture.
LMmdl4VltD4.why: HN commenters cite it as the go-to parody of startup pitch culture whenever buzzword-heavy startups come up.

LQ8Nr3_2724.summary: A short Campus Reform clip in which a teacher claims to have helped write Common Core with the aim of ending white privilege. It is a brief, politically charged advocacy-media piece.
LQ8Nr3_2724.why: HN uses it only as a critical reference in political arguments about Common Core, not as something to recommend.

LRmrMiOWdfc.summary: Google's 2008 press announcement of its open source browser, Chrome, featuring Sundar Pichai among the presenters.
LRmrMiOWdfc.why: Cited as the original Chrome launch event, to show how it stood out against competing browsers.

LRq_SAuQDec.summary: A Red Dwarf clip where Kryten fixes a toaster and finds it to be the most annoying machine in the universe, endlessly offering toast.
LRq_SAuQDec.why: HN uses it as a recurring joke reference whenever threads feature annoying, over-eager smart devices and AI products.

LSHZ_b05W7o.summary: Sony CSL's Daddy's Car is a pop song composed with AI in the style of the Beatles, with lead sheets generated by software from Beatles-style training material. Humans produced, arranged and performed it.
LSHZ_b05W7o.why: Cited as an early example of AI-composed music, usually with the caveat that humans did much of the production.

LSZPNwZex9s.summary: Google Netherlands' April Fools' 2016 video presents a fictional self-driving bicycle for Amsterdam, framed as a serious product launch.
LSZPNwZex9s.why: Used as a joke or as a reference to Google's April Fools pranks and the idea of autonomous bikes, not as something to learn from.

LTJvdGcb7Fs.summary: The original Broadway cast performs 'The Internet Is For Porn' from the musical Avenue Q, with press-reel footage synced to the live performance.
LTJvdGcb7Fs.why: HN commenters post it as a joke when a thread touches on the internet and porn.

LV0wTtiJygY.summary: A very short humorous clip titled 'I used to be with it', playing on the line that they changed what 'it' was. It is a brief meme-style video with no substantive content.
LV0wTtiJygY.why: HN uses it purely as a joke reply about being out of touch with changing trends.

LVsqIjAeeXw.summary: Thunderf00t debunks the Waterseer, a crowdfunded device that claims to condense drinking water from the air using cool ground. He argues the physics does not support its claims.
LVsqIjAeeXw.why: HN cites it as a warning and a debunking whenever water-from-air or similar crowdfunded gadgets appear.

LXb3EKWsInQ.summary: A five-minute 4K 60fps HDR travel montage of Costa Rica by the Mystery Box video team. It is a remastered version of their popular scenic footage.
LXb3EKWsInQ.why: Used as a convenient high-resolution, high-framerate test clip for video decoders, YouTube format handling and power benchmarks.

LXzJR7K0wK0.summary: A short clip from the film Idiocracy showing a hospital reception computer where staff pick a condition from a board of simple pictorial buttons.
LXzJR7K0wK0.why: It is invoked as a joke whenever a product forces users through dumbed-down or unhelpful interfaces and automated support.

L_Guz73e6fw.summary: Lex Fridman's long interview with OpenAI CEO Sam Altman about GPT-4, ChatGPT, and the future of AI. Topics include models as reasoning engines, AI risk, and consciousness.
L_Guz73e6fw.why: HN mostly cites it for specific Altman quotes, such as models as reasoning engines rather than databases, while many commenters found the interview shallow or insincere.

LfmAG4dk-rU.summary: Dashcam-style footage of a Tesla Model 3 crashing into an overturned truck on a highway in Taiwan during the morning commute.
LfmAG4dk-rU.why: HN cites it as an example of Autopilot failures in discussions about the limits of Tesla's driver assistance and self-driving.

LhF_56SxrGk.summary: A two-minute supercut of film and TV characters ordering a computer to 'enhance' a blurry image into a perfectly sharp one. It is a remaster of an earlier 2009 version.
LhF_56SxrGk.why: HN uses it as a punchline in threads about image upscaling and super-resolution, where the movie trope has become partly real.

LkqiDu1BQXY.summary: A clip from Star Trek IV: The Voyage Home where Scotty introduces an astonished engineer to future technology to build the whale tanks.
LkqiDu1BQXY.why: Used as a joke or pop-culture reference in comments about futuristic technology and talking to computers.

LlOSdRMSG_k.summary: A one-minute clip from Mad Men season 5 in which Don Draper tells Michael Ginsberg in an elevator that he doesn't think about him at all.
LlOSdRMSG_k.why: Posted purely as a joke reply to scenes of one party dismissing another, such as rival companies or high-status people brushing off others.

Lp7E973zozc.summary: Mel Robbins gives a TEDxSF talk on why people sabotage themselves and how to push past hesitation. It is the source of her 'count backward from five' technique.
Lp7E973zozc.why: HN mostly cites it in discussions of procrastination and the 5-second rule, not as a strong recommendation.

LqxbsADqDI4.summary: An Apple WWDC24 session introducing Embedded Swift, a subset of Swift with no runtime that targets tiny microcontrollers. It demonstrates the idea on an off-the-shelf Matter smart home device.
LqxbsADqDI4.why: HN cites it as Apple's own explanation of why Embedded Swift exists and what it targets.
